question: Should OpenClaw commit to FreeBSD as an officially supported platform, and if so should it be Tier 1, a narrower community-supported package path, or not planned for now?
rationale: The requested outcome spans release ownership, packaging, supported-platform docs, installers, service management, and CI/release validation, so code automation cannot safely choose the product support promise.

options.title: Define A Scoped Support Tier First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the FreeBSD support tier and owner, then split implementation into release-owned tasks.

options.title: Decline Official FreeBSD Support For Now
options.body: Close the request as not planned and allow community packaging outside the official supported-platform promise.

options.title: Accept Tier 1 FreeBSD
options.body: Sponsor a release-owned workstream for FreeBSD pkg/ports, service management, docs, CI, and release validation before advertising support.

recommendation.title: Define A Scoped Support Tier First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the FreeBSD support tier and owner, then split implementation into release-owned tasks.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes OpenClaw's official platform promise and release scope, and CONTRIBUTING.md lists steipete as the project lead.
